title: Minimum Absolute Difference
statement: The integers in `arr` are all different. Let `d` be the smallest gap `|x - y|` over every two elements `x` and `y` of `arr`. Return all pairs `[a, b]` of elements of `arr` with `a < b` and `b - a = d`. The list must be in ascending order: pairs with a smaller `a` come first.
constraints: All values in arr are distinct
notes:
## Intuition

Comparing every two elements finds the smallest gap in O(n²). After sorting, though, the closest partner of any value is one of its neighbours: anything farther along the sorted order is at least as far away. So the smallest gap is the smallest difference between adjacent sorted values, and every pair achieving it is an adjacent pair. Scanning in sorted order also produces the pairs already in ascending order.

## Approach

1. Sort `arr` in increasing order.
2. Walk the adjacent pairs and keep the least difference in `smallest`.
3. Walk the adjacent pairs again; whenever `arr[i] - arr[i - 1]` equals `smallest`, append `[arr[i - 1], arr[i]]` to `pairs`.
4. Return `pairs`.

## Example 1, step by step

`arr = [4, 2, 1, 3]` sorts to `[1, 2, 3, 4]`. The adjacent differences are `1, 1, 1`, so `smallest = 1`. All three adjacent pairs match, giving `[[1, 2], [2, 3], [3, 4]]`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n log n) for the sort; both scans are O(n).
- Space: O(n) for the output (sorting in place aside).

## Pitfalls

- Sort numerically with `(a, b) => a - b`; JavaScript's default sort compares numbers as strings and puts `10` before `9`.
- Several pairs can share the smallest gap; collect all of them, not just the first.
- Write each pair smaller value first, and the list in sorted order; the expected output is compared exactly.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `smallest` | the least gap between adjacent sorted values |
| `i` | index of the right element of an adjacent pair |
| `pairs` | the answer, built in ascending order |

narration.2: Sort numerically so that each value's closest partner sits right next to it.
narration.3: No gap has been measured yet.
narration.5: Visit every adjacent pair; i is the right element of the pair.
narration.6: Keep the least gap between neighbours: that is the smallest gap overall.
narration.9: pairs collects the answer in ascending order.
narration.10: Walk the adjacent pairs a second time.
narration.11: Does this pair have exactly the smallest gap?
narration.12: Yes: record it with the smaller value first.
narration.15: The pairs were found left to right, so they are already sorted.
